text:
eva: Noticed in the staging dashboard that when many series are pinned the left axis grows and causes the small metric cards to feel cramped. Thinking we should prototype a "unit pill" + keyboard-first interaction rather than relying on hover. Two variants to test: (1) unit pill top-right of chart that is focusable and reveals full unit + aggregation on focus; (2) inline abbreviated ticks (`k`, `M`) with an `abbr` tooltip exposed on keyboard focus.

tom: I prefer the pill for dense layouts. Practical advantage: it's absolutely positioned so it won't push the container. Dev note: when moving it into the legend area on narrow screens, ensure it becomes part of the DOM flow to avoid overlay collisions.

shreya: UX copy: use singular "Unit" on the pill. Example content: "Unit: requests/sec (1m avg)" with the aggregation line in smaller subdued text. For the abbr approach, use `abbr` elements with `title` and also provide `aria-label` on the axis group.

martin: Accessibility: must be keyboard operable. Pill should be role=button, tabindex=0, and aria-expanded toggles the explainer. Also, axis group should have `aria-label` like "Requests per second, unit: req/s". Do NOT hide full label from screen readers with display:none.

eva: Outlier treatment question: do we soft-dim extreme spikes (alpha) or add a subtle cap marker on the axis that points to the true value? Soft-dim is simpler and preserves scale; cap is explicit but can be confused with annotation.

tom: For streaming charts, soft-dim wins — cheap to draw and hit-testing still works. If we implement a cap marker, collapse multiple caps into a density indicator to avoid clutter.

shreya: Copy caution: label the setting as "De-emphasize extreme values (visual only)" and in the tooltip clarify that data is preserved and exact numbers are available on hover/focus. Avoid words like "hide" or "suppress."

martin: Smoothing: default OFF on dashboard timeseries; ON for micro-sparklines. Smoothing should be visual-only; hover shows raw datapoints. Toggle must use `aria-pressed` and an accessible label that changes with state.

eva: Quick CSS proposal for pill mobility:
```css
.chart__unit-pill{position:absolute;right:10px;top:8px;padding:6px 8px;border-radius:6px;background:#fff;border:1px solid #e6e8eb;font-size:12px}
@media (max-width:420px){
  .chart__unit-pill{position:static;margin-left:8px}
}
```

tom: Perf note: dimming is cheap in canvas; if we later add cap markers or density overlays prefer a single overlay layer for markers to keep DOM small.

shreya: UX test plan: recruit 6 participants (3 infra engineers, 2 PMs, 1 accessibility tester). Tasks: 1) find the largest spike in last 24h, 2) identify the unit using keyboard only, 3) confirm the raw value of a de-emphasized spike. Variants: pill + dimming vs inline abbr + dimming. Measure time + accuracy + SR feedback.

martin: Accessibility checklist to include with prototype:
- pill: role=button, tabindex=0, aria-expanded->explainer region
- axis: aria-label with full unit and aggregation window
- ticks: provide aria-valuetext for screen readers (localized number + unit)
- smoothing toggle: aria-pressed and live update of label
- optional aria-live for large spikes with opt-out in settings

eva: Action items:
- tom: mock desktop + mobile pill + abbr states (Wed)
- shreya: two microcopy options for pill + tooltip (Wed)
- martin: a11y pattern doc + aria examples (Wed)
- eva: assemble test plan and recruit participants (Thu)

eva: Thanks team :thumbsup:
